clue.text: Legal principle requiring tree to be clipped

indicators.note: clipping a word trims its tail, so the tree's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the cypress is an evergreen conifer

explanation.surface: Some legal doctrine apparently insists that a tree be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: CY-PRES (Norman French 'as near as possible') lets a court redirect a charitable gift close to the donor's intention.
explanation.definitionFit: Cy-pres is an equity doctrine applied by courts to failed charitable trusts.

clue.text: In the land of yodellers there's huge hit

indicators.note: the letters for huge are placed within the Swiss abbreviation

parts.note: yodelling is Swiss; CH is the international code for Switzerland
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone in the Alps boasts of a mighty blow.
explanation.walkthrough: A COSH is a British word for a short heavy club, and as a verb, to strike with one.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them over the head with a bludgeon.

clue.text: University officer reported? Gamble is associated with him

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we want a name pronounced like the college official

parts.note: a proctor is a disciplinary officer at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A university official seems to have a gambling problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Procter & Gamble is the big consumer-goods firm, founded by William Procter and James Gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The company name pairs the founder Procter with his partner Gamble.

clue.text: One chats about the end of the world

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gossips about the apocalypse.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschaton is the theological term for the final event of divine history.

clue.text: Make-believe incentive with promises of money to come

parts.note: a spur is something that urges one on
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt later

explanation.surface: A fake inducement comes with pledges of future payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious things are false or counterfeit, merely pretended rather than genuine.

clue.text: Classical boy Amos on vessel coming from island

parts.note: puer is the Latin for boy
Tori Amos is an American singer-songwriter
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A youngster named Amos sails off a boat from some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amos' looks like the prophet but is the surname of singer Tori Amos, giving TORI.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Caribbean island Puerto Rico is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Combat is interrupting inactivity

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the little word goes inside

parts.note: rest is a state of inactivity

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks into a period of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: To combat something is to fight against it or oppose it.

clue.text: Made too big a thing of old composer having died

definitions.text: Made too big a thing of

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: An elderly composer's death gets exaggerated coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate or overplay something is to carry it to excess.

clue.text: Officers giving material to workers?

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Someone hands out cloth to labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants are non-commissioned officers in the army or police.

clue.text: Frustrate the spirit

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to thwart or put an end to it
Whisky, the spirit distilled in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Scotch means both to thwart a scheme and the Scottish whisky.

clue.text: Troopers will be troopers? Male duds

parts.note: troopers are soldiers, that is, men
the idiom 'swear like a trooper' makes swearing what troopers do

explanation.surface: Soldiers behave as soldiers do, in men's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duds' is slang for clothes, not failures.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds is informal for clothes, so male clothing is the shop department for men.

clue.text: Garish tat's awful on a female broadcaster, honest!

indicators.note: awful suggests something botched, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: Kate Adie is a well-known BBC correspondent

explanation.surface: Cheap gaudy rubbish on a woman presenter, frankly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges GARISHTATS into STRAIGHTAS; Kate ADIE was the BBC's chief news correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight as a die is an idiom for thoroughly honest and upright.

clue.text: Writer presents piece, getting a bit of work having run into old news agency

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

indicators.note: into places the unit of work and the run inside the agency name

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
the erg is a small unit of work in physics
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An author presents an article having got a little work from a former press agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunter Grass was the German novelist of The Tin Drum, a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: People making cuts, restricting the community? None of us can have everything

definitions.text: None of us can have everything

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the parers enclose the community

parts.note: parers are people who pare or trim
a town is a community

explanation.surface: Cost-cutters are limiting the town, while philosophising that nobody gets it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint holders share property, each having only a portion rather than the whole.

clue.text: Out of control, giving office assistant whipping

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
whipping is slang for stealing, as is nicking

explanation.surface: An office assistant is given a thrashing and loses all composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipping' looks like a beating but means stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a state of panic has lost control of themselves.

clue.text: Poet has put out superior port

indicators.note: put out means ejected, so the letter for superior leaves the poet's name

parts.note: W H Auden was the Anglo-American poet
U means upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: A poet has dismissed some excellent wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen on the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: Cor! A cute flipping dress!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a really sweet frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but signals the rearrangement of CORACUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre someone is to equip or clothe them.

clue.text: Vulgar female supporter turned back

indicators.note: turned back means the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: A woman fan has turned her back, showing poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or lacking style.

clue.text: Secure catch in sea area off Ireland

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed or secure
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Fishermen secure their haul in waters off the Irish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Fastnet is one of the British shipping forecast's sea areas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fastnet is a named sea area off southern Ireland in the shipping forecast.

clue.text: Work centre said to be suitable for voluntary organisation

indicators.note: said means heard rather than read, so the words are sounded

parts.note: piece is a work and core a centre

explanation.surface: A job centre is reckoned fit for a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peace Corps is an American government volunteer programme abroad.

clue.text: Punished a second time to be made pure?

explanation.definitionFit: The word splits as fined again and also means purified.

clue.text: Destroy a game in perverse display of temper

indicators.note: in places the article and the game inside
perverse here means turned the wrong way round

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Wreck a match in a contrary tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' looks like a description of the temper but signals reading the sulk backwards; 'in' then sets the article and rugby union (RU) within that reversed run.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip apart something, a document say, is to destroy it.

clue.text: As to Golden Calf — it's wrong in a religious retreat!

indicators.note: it's wrong says the letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Idolatry in the Bible is condemned in a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Calf was the idol the Israelites worshipped in Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: Castel Gandolfo is the papal summer residence outside Rome.

clue.text: Singers won't want hard material

indicators.note: not wanting a letter means it is dropped

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers
H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencils

explanation.surface: Vocalists will reject tough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is coconut fibre, used to make matting and rope.

clue.text: Hidden part of the body revealed by Pearl

definitions.text: Hidden part of the body revealed by Pearl

parts.words: Hidden part of the body revealed by Pearl
parts.note: in the name Pearl the organ of hearing sits right in the middle, an organ of hearing within

explanation.surface: Some concealed piece of anatomy is exposed by a woman called Pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: The innermost part of the ear holds the cochlea and is hidden within the skull.

clue.text: Extremely drunk, all right, fools all falling over

indicators.note: falling over turns the run upside down, so it reads backwards in this across light

parts.note: OK means all right
nits is British slang for idiots

explanation.surface: Very drunk, and all right, the idiots keep tumbling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is slang for very intoxicated.

clue.text: Get to spa, knackered — support needed at end of drive?

definitions.text: support needed at end of drive?

indicators.note: knackered means broken, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Exhausted, go to a health resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knackered' is British slang for worn out; here it rearranges GETTOSPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatepost carries the gate at the bottom of a driveway.

clue.text: Litre extracted from mixer for drinking session

indicators.note: extracted means removed, so the litre letter leaves the kitchen gadget

parts.note: a blender is a food mixer

explanation.surface: A litre is taken out of the mixing device for a boozy session.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is slang for a prolonged spree of drinking.
